races.name: Racing Welfare Supporting Mental Health Awareness Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Tiger Tobin
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning after 380 days off with headgear applied, needs the run but sits in ideal tactical position behind likely pace battle

runners_data.name: Our Guide
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with excellent recent form including two wins, proven on similar going and distance, clear class advantage with Gavin Sheehan up

runners_data.name: Ka Mate Du Brivet
runners_data.note: Front runner with ability but inconsistent, 51 days since last run could aid freshness, needs to avoid early speed duel with At Sunrise
runners_data.comment: Made a fairly useful rival work quite hard when second (well held in end) on hurdle debut
runners_data.spotlight: Irish point winner; tailed off in a bumper on rules debut in February but made a fairly useful rival work quite hard when second of three (albeit well held in the end) over hurdles at Fontwell (2m5f, good) in March; has another big role to play.

runners_data.name: Savon
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and pulled up last time, major question marks over ability and stamina for this longer trip, 5lb claimer takes off useful weight
runners_data.comment: Pulled up when a big-priced outsider for last month's hurdle debut (2m4f)
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten on bumper debut in March and pulled up when 200-1 for last month's hurdle debut at Ffos Las (2m4f, good to soft).

runners_data.name: At Sunrise
runners_data.note: Confirmed leader but limited ability shown in previous runs, 158 days off track and headgear applied suggests problems, likely pace angle only
runners_data.comment: Pulled up when 300-1 for hurdling debut at Hereford (2m3f) in December
runners_data.spotlight: Safely held in two bumpers last spring and pulled up when 300-1 for hurdling debut at Hereford (2m3f, good to soft) in December.

runners_data.name: Granite Sands
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse but bottom of weights for good reason, modest form figures suggest insufficient class despite 3lb claiming allowance

runners_data.name: Shuil Rocco
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who showed improvement last time at Chepstow, step up to 2m6f unknown but Sean Bowen booking adds confidence
runners_data.comment: Kept on steadily for modest fourth at Chepstow last month; further progress possible
runners_data.spotlight: Bettered hurdle debut when keeping on steadily for modest fourth at Chepstow (2m3f, good) last month; needs to progress again over this longer trip but that's possible.

races.paceDynamic: At Sunrise and Ka Mate Du Brivet will contest the early lead in this small field, with both having confirmed front-running styles that should create an honest gallop from the start. Tiger Tobin sits prominently behind the pace-setters, while Our Guide, Granite Sands and Shuil Rocco will all track from further back looking to pounce late. The sustained pace over 2m6f on good to firm ground will test stamina reserves, particularly as both leaders have questionable finishing kicks. This race shape strongly favours the hold-up horses who can conserve energy and finish powerfully, especially Our Guide with his proven ability to quicken late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If the two front runners At Sunrise and Ka Mate Du Brivet duel early and weaken from 2f out
scenarios.body: The honest pace will set up perfectly for the patient hold-up horses to sweep past tired leaders in the final furlong. Our Guide's proven late kick makes him the primary beneficiary of this likely tactical setup.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Profits
scenarios.trigger: If Tiger Tobin can sit third behind the battling leaders without getting involved in their duel
scenarios.body: He can strike with a well-timed move approaching the final flight while the leaders tire and before the hold-up horses can respond. His prominent style positions him perfectly to exploit any pace collapse.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Ka Mate Du Brivet can establish a clear early lead without At Sunrise pressing him hard
scenarios.body: The classier of the two leaders could maintain a sustainable rhythm and prove too strong for the closers on this sharp track. His second place last time out suggests he has the ability when things fall right.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If both At Sunrise and Ka Mate Du Brivet weaken dramatically after a fierce early battle
scenarios.body: The entire field bunches up turning for home creating a sprint finish where any horse could prevail. Even outsiders like Granite Sands could benefit from the chaotic finish despite their limitations.

watchPoints.text: At Sunrise and Ka Mate Du Brivet could engage in a suicidal early pace battle that sets up the race for the hold-up horses
Tiger Tobin has been off for 380 days and may need this run despite his ideal tactical position behind the leaders
Our Guide's jumping will be crucial given his hold-up style requires clean leaps to maintain position for his late run
Savon pulled up last time and represents a significant unknown quantity at these odds in what could be a tactical affair
The good to firm ground may play against the front runners' stamina over this extended 2m6f trip at Stratford

races.name: Happy 32nd Birthday Lottie Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Captain Cool
runners_data.note: Front-runner returning from 46-day break under Sean Quinlan, needs to prove stamina over this trip with multiple pace rivals pressuring him early

runners_data.name: Whatyouwaitingfor
runners_data.note: Leading front-runner with best recent form and chase experience, Lilly Pinchin can use tactical awareness to control the strong pace scenario
runners_data.comment: Ran well for long way when third at Chepstow last month; dryer ground could suit here
runners_data.spotlight: Remote when second of three on stable/chase debut but ran well for a long way before weakening into third at Chepstow (2m, good to soft) last month and could be better suited by the forecast dryer ground here.

runners_data.name: Definite Dream
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 314-day layoff for Denis Coakley, poor completion rate over fences raises serious reliability concerns
runners_data.comment: Ran quite well on latest hurdling start but makes chase debut after 314-day absence
runners_data.spotlight: 0-9 in points (completed only three times) and has same strike-rate over hurdles; gave a fairly good account when fifth of 15 at Worcester (2m, good) last July but this chasing debut comes after a 314-day absence.

runners_data.name: Alba Crus
runners_data.note: Another pace-setter who showed poor form last time for Warren Greatrex, three leaders in small field creates tactical nightmare for connections
runners_data.comment: Bumper winner; well beaten on handicap hurdle debut but quickly switched to fences
runners_data.spotlight: Good-ground bumper winner who was placed in a 2m3f novice hurdle last season; ran poorly on recent handicap hurdle debut (2m4f) and now has a point to prove but might be aided by first-time tongue-tie here and connections are evidently keen to switch him to fences.

runners_data.name: Miss Denver
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with 11-day turnaround carrying just 147lbs, Sam Twiston-Davies booking suggests stable confidence in testing conditions

runners_data.name: Cawthorne Cracker
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer perfectly suited to strong pace scenario, course winner returning from respectable Market Rasen third 42 days ago
runners_data.comment: Ran okay last month, after a break, but others in this field probably have more potential
runners_data.spotlight: Course winner over hurdles; returned from a break with respectable third in Market Rasen chase (2m1f, good) last month but is 0-5 over fences now and others in this line-up probably have more potential.

runners_data.name: Intenzo
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose free-running style remains a concern despite tactical advantage, Charlie Maggs' 3lb claim helps offset recent disappointing efforts
runners_data.comment: Below form on last two starts; good claims if judged on Sedgefield second in March
runners_data.spotlight: Below form on last two appearances and his tendency to race too freely remains a worry but he made a promising chase/handicap debut when clear second at Sedgefield (2m, good) in March and that form has been well advertised by the winner since; good claims if back at that level.

races.paceDynamic: Captain Cool, Whatyouwaitingfor and Alba Crus will ensure a strong gallop from the start over this testing 2m1f trip at Stratford. With three confirmed front-runners in a small field, they'll carve out a demanding pace that will test stamina reserves in the closing stages. The sustained gallop will suit horses with proven staying power who can finish strongly from off the pace. This race shape clearly favours hold-up horses and prominent racers with strong finishing kicks over pure speed horses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Gallop Collapses Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners go too hard early and tie up in the final furlong
scenarios.body: The blistering pace set by Captain Cool, Whatyouwaitingfor and Alba Crus will find them all out in the closing stages, allowing the hold-up horses to sweep past. Cawthorne Cracker and Intenzo, despite their flaws, will benefit most from this tactical setup with their patient styles.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Whatyouwaitingfor Controls Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Whatyouwaitingfor can dictate a more measured gallop and see off his front-running rivals
scenarios.body: With superior form figures and jockey Lilly Pinchin able to rate him better than his rivals, he can control the tempo and kick clear. His recent chase experience gives him a crucial edge over the other pace-setters who have question marks.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Captain Cool Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Captain Cool can steal a march and maintain a steady rhythm without the others pressuring him early
scenarios.body: The Jennie Candlish-trained gelding gets an uncontested lead and builds an unassailable advantage before the others react. His recent consistency suggests he can handle the tactical scenario if given breathing room.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace Suits All
scenarios.trigger: If the three leaders respect each other and settle into a more conservative rhythm early on
scenarios.body: Without the expected fierce pace battle, the race becomes more tactical and suits horses with tactical speed rather than pure stamina. This levels the playing field significantly and brings more runners into contention late.

watchPoints.text: Alba Crus was declared a non-runner, reducing the pace pressure significantly and changing the entire tactical complexion of this contest
Watch if Captain Cool and Whatyouwaitingfor engage in an early speed duel, as both will be vulnerable to late closers in the final furlong
Intenzo's tendency to race too freely could negate his tactical advantage if he gets involved in the early pace battle despite his hold-up style
Definite Dream's 314-day absence makes him very hard to assess, watch for early signs of fitness or ring rustiness under Brendan Powell
Miss Denver's quick 11-day turnaround following her recent Stratford run could indicate either peak fitness or potential fatigue setting in

races.name: Deryck Baker Memorial Mares' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: I Am The Moon
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who should get uncontested lead but may lack finishing kick when challenged by prominent racers after 36 days off
runners_data.comment: Seemingly back in prime form in February but ended last season with two lesser efforts
runners_data.spotlight: Seemingly back in good nick when winning readily at Doncaster (2m3f, soft) in February but ended last season with two lesser efforts (3m/2m7f) and has questions to answer again over this new trip.

runners_data.name: Jena d'Oudairies
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in first-time blinkers who won last time at Taunton and gets ideal tactical setup tracking the leader
runners_data.comment: Led close home in new blinkers last month; still on a good mark and unexposed as a stayer
runners_data.spotlight: Led close home to score in first-time blinkers at Taunton (3m, good) last month and is now 2-11 over hurdles; not always one to rely upon heavily but remains well handicapped on older form and unexposed as a stayer.

runners_data.name: Dunaden Island
runners_data.note: Prominent racer making rules debut over this extended trip with inexperienced 5lb claimer Rian Corcoran in the saddle
runners_data.comment: Ex-pointer; fourth at big odds on rules debut but well beaten twice since; handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: 1-9 in points; belied triple-digit odds when fourth on rules debut at Wincanton (1m7f, heavy) in February but well beaten twice since (1m7f/2m5f); upped in trip for handicap debut; opening mark demands improvement.

runners_data.name: Mahon Falls
runners_data.note: Prominent racer stepping up significantly in trip to 3m2½f for the first time but has shown consistent placed form at shorter distances

runners_data.name: All Inn Hand
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who won here last year but faces tactical disadvantage as the lone closer in a small field with steady pace
runners_data.comment: Hurdle/chase winner last spring; returned with lacklustre chase run last month
runners_data.spotlight: Won the 2m6f novice hurdle on this card a year ago (good ground) and followed up in handicap chase at Hexham (3m, good to soft) three weeks later, but returned from layoff with lacklustre chase run last month; now reverts to hurdling over new trip and with headgear switched.

races.paceDynamic: I Am The Moon will lead from the outset with no other confirmed front-runners in this small field of five mares. Jena d'Oudairies, Dunaden Island and Mahon Falls are all prominent racers who will track the leader in behind, while All Inn Hand as the sole hold-up performer will be dropped out the back early. The sustainable pace set by I Am The Moon without early pressure will allow the prominent racers to travel comfortably and launch their challenges turning for home. This race shape strongly favours the prominent racers who can sit handy and pounce, rather than the lone leader or the hold-up horse who faces a tactical disadvantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Racers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If I Am The Moon sets a steady pace without being harassed early
scenarios.body: The prominent trio of Jena d'Oudairies, Dunaden Island and Mahon Falls get the perfect trip tracking the leader before mounting their challenges. All Inn Hand from the back faces too much to do against runners who've had easier passages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Kicks Clear Late
scenarios.trigger: If I Am The Moon quickens approaching the final flight and finds extra reserves
scenarios.body: Having travelled smoothly out front, I Am The Moon finds another gear when the prominent racers try to challenge and holds them at bay. The good ground and lack of early pressure plays to the leader's stamina reserves.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Sweeps By
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes crawling throughout
scenarios.body: All Inn Hand benefits from an exceptionally slow gallop that allows Sean Bowen to produce a devastating late run from the rear. The prominent racers get caught flat-footed by the lack of pace and cannot respond to the hold-up challenge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If I Am The Moon goes too slowly and the field bunches up turning in
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the last flight with all five runners still in contention. Superior class and finishing speed becomes paramount rather than tactical positioning throughout the race.

watchPoints.text: All Inn Hand could be trapped at the back if the pace quickens unexpectedly and may struggle to make ground up in time
I Am The Moon's stamina reserves after 36 days off - if the prominent racers pressure early, the leader could fold quickly
Dunaden Island's stepping up in trip with an inexperienced jockey could lead to positioning errors or stamina questions
Jena d'Oudairies has history of being unreliable despite ability - watch for any market confidence
The good to firm ground is faster than some recent runs - watch which horses handle the surface change best

races.name: William Austin 50 Year Celebration Mares' Handicap Chase (Queen Boudicca Mares' Chase Series Qual')

runners_data.name: A Little Something
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning to good ground where she's been runner-up twice recently, including over this trip at Fontwell last month.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up off today's mark on last two appearances; likely contender again
runners_data.spotlight: Pulled up when making chase debut on heavy ground but runner-up twice on good ground since, latterly at Fontwell (2m3f) last month; gets another chance off the same mark here; obvious contender.

runners_data.name: Pure Seduction
runners_data.note: Prominent style with 5lb claimer aboard, trainer hitting 12% strike-rate but hasn't been seen for 52 days which raises fitness concerns.

runners_data.name: Miss Fedora
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer carrying bottom weight who needs the race to develop into a sprint but looked very rusty when pulled up in March for new connections.
runners_data.comment: Started off for new stable with two disappointing runs (chase/hurdle); revival needed
runners_data.spotlight: Dual hurdle and dual chase winner when trained by Seamus Mullins; very disappointing joint-favourite when pulled up in a chase for new stable in March and finished down the field over hurdles last month; needs to turn things around.

runners_data.name: Ballyhiho
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner with first-time tongue-tie fitted, likely to get uncontested lead but trainer's 0-from-5 recent record raises execution concerns.

runners_data.name: Little Wren
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with cheekpieces retained from winning chase debut, but 97 days off and needs strong pace to be effective from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Made all on chasing debut; flopped next time but may still have potential
runners_data.spotlight: Displayed significant improvement when fitted with cheekpieces for chasing debut at Fakenham (2m5f, good to soft) in January, making all to win by just over 7l; lacked fluency and was pulled up at Plumpton (3m1f, soft) the following month but has strong claims if back on song after 97-day break.

races.paceDynamic: Ballyhiho represents the sole confirmed front-runner with lead preference, meaning she'll dictate terms from the outset without early pressure. A Little Something and Pure Seduction both show prominent tendencies but are more likely to track than challenge for the early lead. With Miss Fedora and Little Wren both hold-up performers, the pace will be measured through the early stages before quickening significantly from the second-last fence. This sustainable gallop followed by a sharp injection of pace heavily favours the prominent runners who can position close enough to strike but avoid the front-runner's workload.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Ballyhiho gets an easy lead and stays strongly.
scenarios.body: She controls every call without pressure, saving energy for a sustained kick from two out that the closers cannot match. Her recent form shows steady improvement and she thrives when setting her own fractions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly crawling allowing closers to get involved.
scenarios.body: A Little Something or Pure Seduction can sit in perfect stalking positions before timing their runs to perfection as the race develops into a sprint. The lack of early pace nullifies Ballyhiho's tactical advantage and brings stamina into play.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is stronger than expected with multiple horses pressing.
scenarios.body: Miss Fedora and Little Wren benefit from a genuinely-run race that sets up perfectly for their closing kicks from off the pace. Their class advantage shows when the race becomes a true test of speed and stamina combined.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Ballyhiho faces unexpected early pressure or makes jumping errors.
scenarios.body: The race becomes messy with no clear tactical pattern, allowing any horse with clean jumping and good positioning to capitalize. Form and class become secondary to in-running luck and jockeyship.

watchPoints.text: Ballyhiho's jumping under pressure - any early mistakes will compromise her front-running tactics and open up the race completely.
Pure Seduction's fitness after 52-day break - if she's ring-rusty the 5lb claiming jockey may struggle to get competitive position.
Miss Fedora's attitude early on - her March pulled-up effort suggests confidence issues that could resurface if pressured.
Little Wren's position turning in - she needs to be within striking distance despite hold-up style given the likely lack of pace.
A Little Something's jumping rhythm - she's been consistent on good ground but needs to travel strongly to capitalize on tactical advantage.

races.name: Boss & The Hoggs Live On The 30th May Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Frank Stamper
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who ran his best race recently when second at Fontwell, suggesting current form and tactics align well for this setup
runners_data.comment: 0-6 over hurdles but ran well when close second at Fontwell last month; good chance
runners_data.spotlight: 0-6 over hurdles but ran well when close second at Fontwell (2m1f, good to soft) last month and is probably still on a workable mark after 1lb nudge; good chance.

runners_data.name: Galactic Jack
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse showing improved form for new connections with a third-place finish at Taunton behind Mi Sueno, giving him proven form advantage
runners_data.comment: Best of three runs for new stable when third at Taunton last month; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Useful on the Flat in his prime; 0-8 over hurdles but posted best of three runs for new stable (since a long absence) when third at Taunton (2m, good; behind Mi Sueno) last month and is another 1lb lower here; respected.

runners_data.name: Reteti
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who can bridge the gap between leader and hold-up pack, though 83 days since last run raises fitness questions
runners_data.comment: Ran well for a long way on handicap debut and may be better suited by this faster ground
runners_data.spotlight: 0-13 under all codes but ran well for a long way before weakening into fifth of seven on handicap hurdle debut at Plumpton (2m, soft) in February and ought to be better suited by the forecast faster ground here.

runners_data.name: A Good Yomp
runners_data.note: Strong hold-up performer coming off a recent win just 2 days ago, but quick turnaround could impact recovery

runners_data.name: Prettylady
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare stepping into handicap company off a low mark with cheekpieces applied for the first time
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in three maiden hurdles this year but may fare better in handicaps
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten in three maiden hurdles for new stable in early part of this year but showed some ability on the Flat when trained in France, and the switch to forecast good ground may enable some improvement on this handicap hurdle debut.

runners_data.name: Mi Sueno
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who sets the tactical template but has developed a pattern of fading in the finish
runners_data.comment: Creditable second over hurdles last month but pulled up in a recent chase; hard to predict
runners_data.spotlight: Returned to form with creditable second at Taunton (2m, good) last month, his third start for David Brace, but was pulled up on recent chasing debut and has become hard to predict.

runners_data.name: Blazing Gaden
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with inconsistent recent form and a tendency to find little when asked for effort

runners_data.name: Trooper
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer making handicap debut off basement mark but showing little encouragement in recent maiden hurdles
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in three maiden hurdles but won five times on the Flat in Belgium/Germany
runners_data.spotlight: Five-time Flat winner in Belgium/Germany; well beaten in three maiden hurdles this year (last two runs for current stable) but has basement mark for handicap hurdle debut and is well worth a glance in the betting.

races.paceDynamic: Mi Sueno will take them along from the front in this small field, likely getting an uncontested lead given his clear front-running style against seven hold-up/midfield runners. The pace will be steady rather than searching, allowing Mi Sueno to dictate terms through the early stages without pressure. However, Mi Sueno has a tendency to fade in the finish, which will set up a cavalry charge from the pack of hold-up horses in the home straight. This race shape strongly favours hold-up performers who can finish strongly, as they'll get the perfect setup of a moderate early pace followed by a weakening leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Mi Sueno sets steady fractions and predictably weakens approaching the final flight
scenarios.body: The patient hold-up horses will have plenty left in the tank for a sustained finish, overwhelming the tiring leader. Frank Stamper and A Good Yomp are perfectly positioned to exploit this tactical setup with their strong staying finishes.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Bridges Gap
scenarios.trigger: If Reteti tracks the pace more closely and avoids getting caught too far back
scenarios.body: Reteti's prominent running style allows him to stay in touch with Mi Sueno while the others get further detached. When Mi Sueno weakens, Reteti can strike before the hold-up horses fully wind up their challenges.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Leader Finds Extra Resolve
scenarios.trigger: If Mi Sueno runs more resolutely than recent form suggests and doesn't fade as expected
scenarios.body: His recent second at Taunton showed he can sustain his effort better when the pace isn't too strong. The hold-up horses may leave themselves too much to do if Mi Sueno keeps finding on the run-in.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Favours Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Mi Sueno goes too slow early and the race becomes a tactical crawl
scenarios.body: The lack of pace pressure early on turns this into a sprint finish where the horses with the most natural speed will prevail. The proven faster horses like Frank Stamper and Galactic Jack benefit most from this tactical development.

watchPoints.text: Mi Sueno's early pace-setting - if he goes too fast early he'll stop even more dramatically than usual in the finish
A Good Yomp's recovery from his win just 2 days ago - quick turnarounds can significantly impact jumping horses' performance
Reteti's fitness after 83 days off - his prominent style requires race sharpness to be effective against this field
Frank Stamper's jumping under pressure - his hold-up style requires clean hurdling to maintain momentum in the finish
Galactic Jack's ability to reproduce his Taunton third - that form gives him a concrete advantage over several of these rivals

races.name: Ladies Day On Sunday 19th July Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Tapley
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with class edge but 33 days off and apprentice jockey reduces winning chances

runners_data.name: Jubilant
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 46-day break with disappointing recent form since emphatic Plumpton win
runners_data.comment: Back from break with two disappointing runs towards end of last season; has bit to prove
runners_data.spotlight: Ended 2025 with emphatic win from the front at Plumpton (3m1f, good to soft), his third chase success, but returned from break with two disappointing runs (chase/hurdle) towards end of last season and has something to prove.

runners_data.name: King Roly
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in excellent form with winning recent record and strong jockey-trainer combination
runners_data.comment: Three chase wins in early part of last season; ran okay last month, after a break; player
runners_data.spotlight: Won three small-field chases in early part of last season (2m3f-2m4f, good) and ran better than eventual 18l defeat suggests at Perth (2m4f, good; hampered by final-fence faller) last month, after a layoff; will be fine over today's longer trip and goes on the shortlist.

runners_data.name: Diplomatic Ash
runners_data.note: Non-runner
runners_data.comment: Not at best when making the frame on his two starts in March; others appeal more
runners_data.spotlight: Finished weakly when well-held fourth at Kempton (3m, good) in March and was also below best at Ascot (2m5f, good; refitted cheekpieces) later that month, where he plugged on from a long way off the pace to take a modest second; current mark is workable but others appeal more.

runners_data.name: Grillon De Monty
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning after 196-day absence but dual course winner with hooded headgear applied
runners_data.comment: Dual Worcester chase winner last summer; absent since poor hurdle run in November
runners_data.spotlight: Dual chase winner at Worcester (2m7f, good) last summer; absent since heavy defeat over hurdles in November, though, and resumes on fairly tough mark; hooded for first time.

runners_data.name: Okavango Delta
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 146-day layoff but has winning record fresh and stays the trip well
runners_data.comment: Off since December but has good record when fresh and Sean Bowen is booked
runners_data.spotlight: Absent since below-par run in December but returned from break with creditable second at Musselburgh (2m, good to soft; stays much further) in November and won when fresh last spring; has travelled from Northumberland for this race and Sean Bowen is booked; interesting.

runners_data.name: Bagheera Ginge
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner returning after 210-day break with visor fitted and strong stable backing

runners_data.name: Arrycan
runners_data.note: Prominent runner wearing new cheekpieces but 12-year-old veteran needs significant improvement from recent efforts
runners_data.comment: Ex-Irish veteran; safely held on both stable starts; cheekpieces now tried
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-Irish veteran who was safely held on first two starts for new stable this spring (both 3m, good); needs good boost from new cheekpieces here.

races.paceDynamic: Bagheera Ginge will dictate the gallop from the front, with King Roly, Tapley and several other prominent runners tracking close behind creating a competitive early pace. The sustained tempo over 2m6½f on good to firm ground will test stamina reserves in the closing stages. With multiple prominent runners pressuring the leader and no genuine hold-up horses except Jubilant and Okavango Delta, this becomes a test of who can quicken best from the pace. This race shape favours prominent runners who can track the gallop and have a turn of foot, rather than the front-runner or hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If King Roly, Tapley or Grillon De Monty track Bagheera Ginge perfectly and produce late kick
scenarios.body: The sustained pace sets up perfectly for horses positioned second or third who can outstay the leader. King Roly's recent winning form and Tapley's class advantage become decisive factors.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Bagheera Ginge gets an uncontested lead and the pace becomes too steady early
scenarios.body: The lack of early pressure allows the leader to conserve energy for a strong finish over this stamina-sapping trip. Twiston-Davies' tactical nous helps Bagheera Ginge repel late challenges from tired pursuers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes genuinely strong with multiple prominent runners competing
scenarios.body: Jubilant and Okavango Delta get the perfect setup as the pace-makers tie up in the final furlong. Their fresh finishing kicks prove superior to battle-weary leaders.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Takes Advantage
scenarios.trigger: If the favourites fail to settle or encounter trouble in running
scenarios.body: Arrycan's new cheekpieces provide the needed improvement while others disappoint. The veteran's experience at the trip becomes crucial in a messy race.

watchPoints.text: Bagheera Ginge must handle the 210-day absence as any rustiness will be exposed by the competitive pace
King Roly could get trapped behind horses if the pace becomes stop-start given his prominent running style
Jubilant needs to overcome his recent poor form to justify the hold-up tactics that this race shape could favour
Grillon De Monty faces a fitness test after nearly seven months off despite his course-winning credentials
Tapley's inexperienced jockey Isabelle Ryder must judge the pace perfectly from a prominent position

races.name: Family Day On Sunday 12th July Open Maiden National Hunt Flat Race (Category 3 Elimination) (GBB)

runners_data.name: Scotto
runners_data.note: Highest rated but lightly raced with unknown running style and Sean Bowen booking suggests expectations despite lack of public form
runners_data.comment: Trainer has good bumper strike-rate (17%) and has booked Sean Bowen for this newcomer
runners_data.spotlight: Sixth foal; brother to hurdle/chase winner Brayhill, half-brother to useful hurdler Chooseyourweapon and a point winner; dam pulled up in points, out of a useful bumper/jumps winner; trainer has pretty good bumper strike-rate (17%) and has booked Sean Bowen for this newcomer.

runners_data.name: Law Of The Jungle
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits but concerning recent form including a pull-up at Taunton, though 54-day break allows recovery time
runners_data.comment: Pulled up when 100-1 for British debut at Taunton in March
runners_data.spotlight: Only eighth of nine on debut in France in summer 2024 and pulled up when reappearing for new stable at Taunton (good; 100-1) in March.

runners_data.name: Lightsoutandaway
runners_data.note: Unknown style but respectable recent debut fourth at Fontwell gives solid form reference, good ground conditions suit
runners_data.comment: Just a respectable fourth on recent Fontwell debut but ought to have learnt from that
runners_data.spotlight: Brother to a Listed Flat winner; just a respectable fourth of nine on recent debut at Fontwell (good) but contests what looks another modest race here and ought to have learnt from that experience.

runners_data.name: Bound For Glory
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with consistent fourth-place efforts on good ground, form modest but reliable for this grade
runners_data.comment: Fourth on both starts, latterly at Hereford (good) last month; in the mix again here
runners_data.spotlight: Out of a fair Flat/hurdle winner; fourth on both starts, more recently on good ground at Hereford last month; that form isn't anything to go wild about but he'll probably be on the premises again here.

runners_data.name: Mac's Max
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning from 162-day absence but promising debut second to subsequent hurdle winner provides form foundation
runners_data.comment: Off since well held in December; big player if judged on promising debut in November
runners_data.spotlight: Flat-bred 4yo; absent since disappointing run on soft ground in December but made promising debut when second to a subsequent hurdle winner at Newcastle (good to soft) in November, and that performance makes him of strong interest here.

runners_data.name: Angel Of My Dreams
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but fading tendencies, addition of hood and tongue-tie suggests connections seeking improvement trigger
runners_data.comment: Won a point bumper on debut but well beaten in both subsequent rules bumpers
runners_data.spotlight: Made all in a point bumper in March 2025 but well beaten in two rules bumpers last season; not written off just yet but needs addition of hood/tongue-tie to make a big difference.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front runner in this small field, the early pace will likely be modest with Scotto and Lightsoutandaway potentially drifting forward by default. The hold-up quartet of Law Of The Jungle, Bound For Glory, Mac's Max and Angel Of My Dreams will be content to settle behind, creating a bunched field turning for home. This sets up a sprint finish from the final three furlongs where tactical positioning and late acceleration become crucial. This race shape strongly favours horses with proven finishing kicks who can quicken off a steady pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tactical Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays modest and the field remains bunched into the straight
scenarios.body: The race becomes a test of pure finishing speed where horses like Lightsoutandaway and Mac's Max can unleash their best work. Bound For Glory's consistent form also suits this scenario where tactical speed matters more than stamina.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Scotto Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Scotto uses his class advantage to dictate from the front
scenarios.body: His higher OR of 120 allows him to string out the field at his preferred tempo, making it difficult for the hold-up horses to close. Sean Bowen's tactical nous becomes crucial in judging the right moment to quicken.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Slow Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes crawling slow with no one willing to lead
scenarios.body: The race turns into a messy scramble where positioning and luck in running become paramount over pure ability. Angel Of My Dreams could benefit from the addition of headgear in such a scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Mac's Max Returns Fresh
scenarios.trigger: If Mac's Max shows significant improvement from his 162-day break
scenarios.body: His promising debut form when second to a subsequent hurdle winner suggests untapped potential that could surface after the lengthy absence. The good ground conditions match his preferred surface from that encouraging Newcastle run.

watchPoints.text: Mac's Max market support given his long absence - any significant shortening suggests stable confidence in his return
Scotto's early positioning will reveal his running style and dictate the race tempo for this small field
Angel Of My Dreams headgear changes taking effect early could signal improved focus and competitiveness
Law Of The Jungle's jumping action after his Taunton pull-up - any signs of reluctance would be concerning
Lightsoutandaway's positioning from his claimer - Freddie Mitchell's tactical decisions will shape his chance
